the acceleration of positrons outwards from a pulsar's magnetic polar cap is dominated by the production of photons of energy \[gsim]1 GeV in the electromagnetic showers of ultra-relativistic electron–positron pairs incident on the stellar atmosphere.

the nature and the mode of acceleration of plasma moving outwards from the surface of the neutron star in the magnetic polar cap are determined not by ion emission or by magnetic conversion of curvature or backward moving photons, but by the hadronic photoabsorbption of photons emitted by the ultra-relativistic electron showers incident on the stellar magnetosphere.

the properties of the plasma are determined not by the acceleration mechanism at the polar cap, but by the properties of the electromagnetic showers incident on the stellar surfaces.
